Which of the following is a possible cause of algorithmic bias?
options: Past discriminatory tendencies reflected in the data

questions.question: Which principle means that an AI system should not unjustly discriminate against a particular person or group?
Which principle is most closely related to handling personal information appropriately?
Which principle is concerned with being answerable when an AI system produces an incorrect or unfair result?
Algorithmic bias can result from biased training data.
If an AI's decision-making process is unclear, this can be called a black-box problem.
Explainable AI helps humans understand why an AI made a particular judgment.
Privacy is not important when using face-recognition technology.
AI responsibility is always clearly assigned before an AI system is used.
Match each situation with the correct AI ethics principle: A Fairness, B Transparency, C Privacy protection, D Accountability.

items.text: A hiring AI evaluates applicants fairly regardless of gender.
The company explains how the AI reached its decision.
Personal information is not used for an unrelated purpose.
Someone is answerable when an AI system produces an incorrect result.

questions.question: For each situation (a-d), indicate which ethical issue is most closely related: A Algorithmic bias, B Privacy, C Black-box problem, D Accountability.

items.text: An AI gives lower scores to one group because the training data contained historical discrimination.
A face-recognition system collects and stores people's facial information.
People cannot understand why an AI made a particular decision.
It is unclear who should take responsibility when an AI system makes an incorrect decision.

questions.question: A company uses an AI system to select candidates for job interviews. The company discovers that the AI gives lower scores to applicants of a particular gender. What ethical issue might this be, what could have caused it, and suggest one action the company could take.
questions.model_answer: This may be algorithmic bias or unfairness. It could be caused by biased or incomplete training data or past discriminatory patterns in the data. The company could review and improve the training data and test the system for fairness across different groups.

questions.question: A school wants to install face-recognition cameras to automatically record student attendance. Give one advantage, one privacy concern, and one rule the school should follow to protect students.
questions.model_answer: An advantage is faster and easier attendance recording. A privacy concern is that students can be identified or tracked using facial data. The school should clearly explain how the data is collected, stored, and used and protect the students' personal information.

questions.question: Face-recognition technology may improve safety and convenience in public places, but it can also create privacy concerns. Explain how convenience, safety, and privacy protection should be balanced.
questions.model_answer: The benefits of safety and convenience should be considered together with possible privacy risks. Only necessary information should be collected, its use should be clearly explained, and personal information should be protected.

questions.question: Analyze how algorithmic bias can arise and how it can be reduced. In your answer, refer to training data and at least two of the principles of AI ethics.
questions.model_answer: Algorithmic bias can arise from biased or incomplete training data, past discrimination, inappropriate variables, proxy variables, or model design. It can be reduced by improving and testing the data and applying principles such as fairness, transparency, privacy protection, and accountability.
